# `max-length-decreased`

maxLength decreased

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` in requests, `info` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `max-length-decreased` (both directions), `max-length-decreased-in-request`, `max-length-decreased-in-response` |
| **Status** | Planned (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

`maxLength` decreased.

## Why this default

In requests: longer strings are rejected. In responses: clients receive shorter strings, which is safe.

## Example

From test case [`recursive-self-reference`](../../test/cases/recursive-self-reference/): A schema that refers to itself through items. A change inside it is found once, without looping.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
+           maxLength: 100
          children:
            type: array
```

Findings:

- `max-length-decreased-in-response` · info · #/components/schemas/TreeNode

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  max-length-decreased: info
```

## How to fix

Keep the old maximum in requests.
